features.name: Occator Crater
features.description: Occator Crater contains the brightest spots on Ceres. These spots are highly reflective deposits of sodium carbonate salts, left behind when briny water from a deep subsurface reservoir erupted and evaporated in the vacuum of space.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: The bright spots are known as Cerealia Facula and Vinalia Faculae.

features.name: Ahuna Mons
features.description: Ahuna Mons is a massive, isolated cryovolcano (ice volcano) that rises sharply from the surrounding terrain. Unlike Earth volcanoes that spew molten rock, Ahuna Mons likely erupted a briny mixture of water ice and salts.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: It is the largest known cryovolcano in the inner solar system.

features.name: Kerwan Crater
features.description: Kerwan is the largest confirmed impact crater on Ceres. It is exceptionally shallow for its size, suggesting that the ice-rich crust of Ceres has relaxed and flattened over billions of years.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Kerwan is so smooth and shallow that it lacks a distinct central peak, typical for craters of this size.

features.name: Dantu Crater
features.description: Dantu is a large, prominent impact crater in the northern hemisphere with a complex central ridge structure. Its interior shows evidence of multiple geological processes including impacts and possible fluid activity.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Named after the Ghanaian god associated with the planting of corn.

features.name: Ezinu Crater
features.description: Ezinu is a large crater in the northern mid-latitudes, notable for its well-preserved rim and the complex terrain of the surrounding region. It sits within the Ezinu quadrangle, one of the most geologically active regions of Ceres.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Named after the Sumerian goddess of grain.

features.name: Haulani Crater
features.description: Haulani is a relatively young crater exhibiting striking bright ejecta rays and a polygonal shape. The bright material is thought to be freshly exposed ice and salts that haven't yet been darkened by space weathering.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Its sharp, straight edges (polygonal shape) indicate it was formed in a crust riddled with pre-existing faults.

features.name: Yalode Crater
features.description: Yalode is the second-largest confirmed crater on Ceres. It features a complex central ridge and is located near another large crater, Urvara, dominating the southern hemisphere's topography.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Fractures crossing Yalode's floor suggest tectonic activity occurred after the impact.

features.name: Urvara Crater
features.description: Urvara is a prominent crater with a central peak and sharp terraces. Together with Yalode, it is one of the most prominent features in Ceres' southern hemisphere.

details.label: Fun Fact
details.value: Urvara has a prominent central ridge that rises over 3 km from the crater floor.
